doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Listening to Skyscraper with Flip Phillips
summary: They play a recording of the tune Bauer wrote, with Davy Tough's four-bar solo, and talk about the record.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me play something for you.
[audio interlude]
I mentioned it. Does Davy Tough take a solo here? It’s a four bar solo.
I love that chord in there by the way, that one little —
[scats]
It’s pretty modern for the time.
How’d you get that? Oh you knew I was coming so you—
I knew you were coming. Actually it comes off this particular recording.
Did you interview him?
Yes we did.
Yeah, I remember this record. Well I don’t know if I’m on all of them.
You’re on this recording, yes.
The whole record?
A lot of it.
Oh yeah? I was sick. One guy, on one of these tunes, he and I stayed on the same two notes through the whole release or something. So he says lookit what he did, he played a flat nine—
Oh yeah, I see what you’re saying.
All he did was analyze it.
He says oh yes, this is a very complex thinking process right? And you were just like —
I didn’t know what else to do.
I love that stuff.
You know it’s sort of frumpy, but at that time, it’s swinging.
It’s swinging.
Yeah.
And Chubby’s on this too.
Chubby isn’t on this one.
He’s on some of the tunes. This is like a kind of a collection of Flip’s, but they’re mostly from forty—
Did he say I wrote that tune?
Yup, sure does.
Because he called me up after he read the book and he says, “You didn’t put my name on it.” I says, “Look at the other page.”
Oh, check it out.
[audio interlude]
That’s wild. Did you write all that out?
I guess I did. I don’t know. I don’t know about a drum solo.
I don’t know what happened to the drum solo.
I don’t know either. Well he says it’s the one tune, that’s the only four bar drum solo that Davy ever took.
Was there other recordings of that tune, probably.
I don’t know.
Well we’ll have to research that.
